messages:
Ava Nguyen: Hey everyone — stuck on local setup, can someone point me at the right person?
Ava Nguyen: postgres comes up fine but my app can't connect to Redis running in compose.
Ava Nguyen: docker-compose snippet I have:
```yaml
services:
  app:
    build: .
    environment:
      - REDIS_HOST=host.docker.internal
  redis:
    image: redis:6.2
    ports:
      - 6379:6379
    network_mode: host
```
Ava Nguyen: App error: redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to host.docker.internal:6379. Tried host.docker.internal and localhost.
Ava Nguyen: I'm on macOS Sonoma, Docker Desktop 4.25 (M1). Who should I ping for infra help?
Samir Patel: don't use network_mode: host on mac — it causes the container to bind differently and host.docker.internal becomes unreliable for container-to-container.
Samir Patel: Remove network_mode, expose the port normally, and set REDIS_HOST to the compose service name (redis).
Samir Patel: quick try: update env -> REDIS_HOST=redis  then: `docker-compose up -d --build`
Toni Morales: also add depends_on: - redis for the app so compose starts order, and ideally a healthcheck so the app waits until redis is ready.
Toni Morales: example healthcheck snippet:
```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
  interval: 5s
  retries: 5
```
Jade Li: On M1, some prebuilt images can behave odd; if you see exec format errors try `redis:7-alpine` or set `platform: linux/amd64` if needed.
Jade Li: also: host.docker.internal is for host<->container; containers talking to each other should use the internal service DNS (the service name).
dev-bot: Helpful doc: https://intranet.redwood.com/dev/local-dev-databases (contains recommended compose patterns for new hires)
Ava Nguyen: Removed network_mode and switched REDIS_HOST to `redis` — works now! :tada: App can connect, migrations ran.
Samir Patel: nice. If you want, I can PR a tiny note in the new-hires README about the redis healthcheck.
Ava Nguyen: yes please. Also — shortcut question: I sometimes only want to run migrations without the whole stack. any tips?
Toni Morales: `docker-compose run --rm app sh -c "npm run migrate"` (or your manage command). That runs the app image without bringing up the full stack. If it needs DB you can attach `--service-ports` or run a quick postgres instance.
Ava Nguyen: perfect, thanks all. Closing thread.
